title: MissionForge shared definitions
description: Definitions shared by every MissionForge data schema. Custom annotations: x-id marks a field that declares an ID of the named kind; x-ref marks a field that references an ID (or a string key) of the named kind; x-value-groups lists the numeric groups of an object that must be tagged in its value_types; x-data-files lists the files under data/ that a schema validates. Other validators ignore these keywords; tools/validate-data.mjs uses them for cross-checks.

string_key.description: Key of a player-visible string in data/strings/<lang>.json. Dot-separated segments, for example part.eng_kerolox_workhorse.name.

value_type.description: Provenance of a numeric value group (design section 19): physical = a physical constant or the result of a physical model; real_world_approximate = rounded from real hardware or real missions; game_value = tuned for balance, not a real figure.

snake_id.description: Lowercase snake_case identifier. Never changes once merged.

part_id.description: Part option ID: lowercase snake_case with a category prefix, for example eng_kerolox_workhorse. Never changes once merged.

part_ref.description: Reference to a part option ID declared in data/parts/.

contract_ref.description: Reference to a contract ID declared in data/contracts.json.

minigame_id.description: Minigame ID as written in design section 10.5, for example MG-01, MG-08b, MG-10a.

minigame_ref.description: Reference to a minigame ID declared in data/minigames.json.

fact_id.description: Fact ID as written in design section 12.4, for example F01. Not a flight phase: phases use the same letter (F0 to F14) but live in fields named phase or flight_phases.

fact_ref.description: Reference to a fact ID declared in data/facts.json.

role_id.description: Mission Control role ID: the console call sign in capitals, for example FLIGHT.

role_ref.description: Reference to a role ID declared in data/roles.json.

boost_ref.description: Reference to a boost ID declared in data/boosts.json.

test_ref.description: Reference to a test ID declared in data/tests.json.

anomaly_ref.description: Reference to an anomaly card ID declared in data/anomalies.json.

part_category.description: Part category. Equals the file name data/parts/<category>.json and maps to one option table of design section 7.

propellant.description: Propellant combination: RP1_LOX (kerolox), LH2_LOX (hydrolox), CH4_LOX (methalox), A50_N2O4 (hypergolic storable), SOLID.

failure_mode.description: Failure mode from the failure model in design section 8.4.

flight_phase.description: Flight phase from design section 9.1 (F0 rollout to F14 debrief; F7b is the parallel booster return).

severity.description: Design review severity (design sections 6.9 and 6.11): blocker = cannot fly, major = high risk, minor = advisory.

flag.description: Snake_case marker for a qualitative effect that Core must act on but for which the design gives no number, for example no_eastward_launch. Every flag in data must be implemented or deliberately ignored by Core.

design_notes.description: Designer-facing notes. Never shown to players.

params_map.description: Named numeric or boolean parameters. Names are snake_case and carry a unit suffix where the value has a unit (window_s, margin_fraction).

effect.description: One numeric effect on a vehicle, mission or session metric. Core combines effects on the same target as (base x product of mul x (1 + sum of add_fraction)) + sum of add.

target.description: Metric affected. The unit of an add value is the suffix of the target name: dry_mass_t (t), cost_M, budget_M and test_cost_M (game $M), lead_days, integ_days and schedule_days (days), delta_v_m_s (m/s), insertion_error_km, landing_ellipse_km and position_error_km (km), launch_window_min (minutes), maneuver_propellant_kg (kg), data_GB (GB), crew_morale_points and score_points (points). reliability, cost_refund_fraction, load_margin, heat_margin, uncertainty_band, guidance_precision and science_value are dimensionless (fractions of 1).

op.description: add = value is added in the unit of the target (reliability -0.003 means minus 0.3 percentage points); add_fraction = relative change, value is a fraction of the base (-0.15 means minus 15%); mul = value is a dimensionless multiplier (0.88 means x0.88).

value.description: Magnitude, copied from the design table. Percentages are stored as fractions.

scope.description: What the effect applies to. Omit when the target is unambiguous. stage = the stage the part is installed on.

condition.description: Condition under which the effect applies. recovered = only if the hardware is recovered in flight.

value_type.description: Provenance of this value when it differs from the tag of the enclosing group.

note_key.description: Optional player-visible explanation of the effect.

criterion.description: One measurable condition on a mission, build or career metric.

metric.description: Metric name in snake_case with a unit suffix where it has a unit (apogee_km, data_downlinked_GB). Each metric used in data must be implemented by Core.

op.description: Comparison: gte, gt, lte, lt and eq compare the metric with value; within means |metric - value| <= tolerance; is_true and is_false test a boolean metric.

value.description: Threshold or target, in the unit named by the metric suffix.

tolerance.description: Allowed deviation from value for op within, same unit as value.

minigame.description: Minigame the metric refers to, for metrics about one minigame result.
